text:
maya: Heads-up: hit a reproducible kvcache indexing wrap on H100 with long contexts (>500k tokens). Memory climbs and evictions point at the wrong slot. Repro attached below. :eyes:

ben: Can you paste the repro steps and a small log snippet?

maya: Repro command: `TEST_SEED=42 ./bench_long_context --model=redwood-lite --tokens=600000 --device=h100`
Logs: 
```
[2026-03-05 14:12:01] kvcache: alloc_page id=4294967294 -> success
[2026-03-05 14:12:01] kvcache: alloc_page id=4294967295 -> success
[2026-03-05 14:12:02] kvcache: alloc_page id=4294967296 -> ERROR: index 0 (wrapped) assigned to new page
[2026-03-05 14:12:02] kvcache: eviction chose slot 0 but slot was live for other stream
```
Seems like page id increments wrap at 2^32 and we index into page table with the raw id (mod table_size) so old pages get clobbered.

oleg: That log screams uint32 overflow. I think pager uses uint32_t for global_page_id. On H100 we're hitting high token counts because of batching + long-history tests. We should switch to uint64_t for the monotonically increasing id. Also add a generation counter to the page table entry to detect stale references.

sarah: FWIW, I ran same repro on A100 and didn't hit the wrap in 24h, but saw fragmentation grow steadily. On RTX6000 it reproduces but with different timing (fragmentation > evict wrap). Might be allocator alignment/large-page behavior across drivers.

perf-bot: Regression detected on master (commit 87f3a2): kvcache eviction latency +12% over 7-day perf window. See: https://perf.internal/runs/87f3a2 (investigating) :warning:

ben: Short-term mitigations? Cap max context or guard increment before indexing?

maya: Quick workaround in my local branch: clamp next_page_id at (1ULL<<48) and add a rebase routine to compact the table when we approach the cap. Not ideal but buys time.

oleg: Proposed proper fix patch (sketch):
```
// use 64-bit generation-aware ids
atomic_uint64_t next_page_id;
struct pte { uint64_t page_id; uint16_t gen; ... };
uint64_t page_id = atomic_fetch_add(&next_page_id, 1);
size_t idx = page_id & page_table_mask; // still mask, but check generation
if (page_table[idx].page_id != page_id) {
  // detect stale entry and avoid clobber without CAS
}
```
We also need to ensure eviction scans use epoch-based reclamation to avoid ABA.

derek: Do we have a small unit test that deterministically forces wrap/race? If so we should add it to eng-runtime CI + a stress job in releases pipeline.

maya: There's a failing repro test in tests/kvcache/test_paged_eviction.cpp that I can extend to force monotonic id overflow with an injectable hook. I'll push a PR in a few hours.

ben: Please open a perf/regress ticket and attach CI reproducer + trace. Schedule a 20m sync with runtime, infra, and ML folks to prioritize.

maya: Will do. Adding TODOs: 1) patch to uint64+gen, 2) add deterministic overflow test, 3) run cross-gpu stress (H100/A100/RTX) and post results, 4) consider compacting table in warm restart.

oleg: Also add a small telemetry metric for "page_id_highwater" so we can alert before we get close to any cap.

maya: Thanks — I'll post the PR and a short perf trace once I have the run. :thumbsup:
